prompt: Order these moments in Mexican history from earliest to latest

items.text: Fall of Tenochtitlan to Cortés and allies
Battle of Puebla (the original Cinco de Mayo)
Madero's call to revolt starts the Mexican Revolution

explanation: Nearly six centuries in five steps: an island city, a conquest, a shout for independence, a surprise win over France, then a revolution.

source.title: Gob.mx / Memórica: fundación de México-Tenochtitlan
source.verification: Gob.mx page says historians agree the founding was in 1325. Ciencia UNAM (ciencia.unam.mx/leer/1102) dates the fall with Cuauhtémoc's capture on 13 Aug 1521. gob.mx/defensa document dates the Grito to the early hours of 16 Sep 1810. INAH Museo del Caracol (lugares.inah.gob.mx/en/node/4240) and bicentenariobc.gob.mx chronology describe Zaragoza's 1862 victory at Puebla. Library of Congress timeline (loc.gov/exhibits/mexican-revolution-and-the-united-states/timeline.html) says Madero's Plan of San Luis Potosí called for an uprising on 20 Nov 1910. Checked 2026-10-27.

source.verification: INAH catalogue: cathedral construction began 1573 and was concluded 1813. INBA (inba.gob.mx/prensa/22803) : Palacio de Bellas Artes inaugurated 29 Sep 1934. CDMX tourism (mexicocity.cdmx.gob.mx/venues/torre-latinoamericana) : construction 1948 to 1956, tallest in the city from 1956. Chapultepec/Cultura and INAH (mna.inah.gob.mx) : museum inaugurated 17 Sep 1964, built in 19 months. Checked 2026-10-27.
